I wrote `shapes.judgements.json` beside the evidence. I haven't run it through `gnd`, so the CLI hasn't checked it yet.

| Group | Verdict |
|---|---|
| g0 | `skip` |
| g1 | `skip` |
| g2 | `many-to-many` |
| g3 | `skip` |
| g4 | `skip` |

The file's `evidence_sha256` is `24c9df25…5b10`, taken from the evidence file's raw bytes. The rationales contain no standalone numbers, because `show_values` is false.

**g3:** you said its second value is an entry error. Correct the population, then run `gnd discover` again to make new evidence. A shapes file can't declare the attribute single-valued. This file's evidence binding will also stop matching once the population changes.

**Next commands:** use the same model, population, `--min-support` (20) and disclosure settings that made the evidence. Fill in the uppercase placeholders.

```sh
gnd discover model.orm.yaml POPULATION --families fact-type --min-support 20 --type-evidence-in evidence.json --shape-judgements shapes.judgements.json --out proposal.json --report report.json --actor ACTOR --requested-at TIMESTAMP
gnd evolve preview model.orm.yaml proposal.json --workspace WORKSPACE --records RECORDS --out preview.json --policy additive
```

If you correct the population first, run the `gnd discover` command that makes new evidence, then judge again before using these commands. If other groups need `gnd-judge-fact-types`, add its file with `--duplicate-judgements` to the first command.

Only g2 is rendered as a proposal, a binary fact type with a uniqueness over both roles. The four skips are counted under `skipped.judged_skip`.
